summary: RidePact hardening-pass backend test — 21/21 total (Node suite 10/10 via `cd /app/backend && npm test` + new Python suite 11/11 covering the new endpoints and flag persistence). Verified: POST /groups/:id/start requires booker (403 for non-booker) and only works on a booked group (409 on 'grouped' status → passes after book). POST /groups/:id/delay by booker succeeds. POST /groups/:id/remove-rider {userId} decrements memberCount and is 403 for non-booker. POST /fares/:groupId/dispute {kind:'payment'|'fare'} sets FareRecord.paymentDisputed / fareDisputed AND RideGroup.adminFlag → group surfaces under GET /admin/resolutions.paymentDisputes / .fareDisputes; admin POST /admin/resolutions/payment|fare/:groupId/resolve clears both. Lifecycle guard: completing a completed group returns 409; non-booker book/start = 403. Booking-info-missing: booking a group whose booker's ride lacks flightInfo + pickupLocation lands the group in /admin/resolutions.missingInfo; POST /admin/resolutions/missing-info/:groupId/resolve clears adminFlag + bookingInfoMissing (verified with a re-GET). No-booker path: booker leaving before booking clears bookerId and surfaces the group in resolutions.bookerNeeded; POST /admin/resolutions/booker/:groupId/assign {userId} promotes the assignee and drops the flag. Cab-cancelled path: POST /groups/:id/cab-cancelled while a fare exists reopens the group (status 'open') and, on a subsequent join, marks the existing fare fareChanged=true (stale). Fare re-entry: POST /fares/:groupId with a new totalCost sets fareChanged=true, PRESERVES the confirming rider's paymentConfirmed=true, and shares re-sum to the new total (80). Payment confirm sets paymentConfirmed. Matching: happy path still works (Node suite covers create → match → join → book → fare → confirm → start → complete → rate + duplicate 409). Capacity 5th join → 409 (Node). All riders leaving auto-cancels the group ('Cancelled' in admin view). Admin RBAC still enforced (student → 403 on /admin/*). Frontend NOT tested per scope.

minor.issue: Node suite (tests/api.test.js line ~44 and phase-2/3 pytest files) treats register as returning 200, but the endpoint actually returns 201. The Node suite still passes because it only reads .accessToken indirectly, but any strict==200 assertion elsewhere would break. Ensure downstream consumers accept 201.

In `mapGroup` (admin.js line 232) the exposed `_id` is used to correlate groups in resolutions arrays, but the RideGroup-level `delayed`, `bookingInfoMissing`, `noBookerFlag`, `adminFlag`, and `rematchNeeded` fields are NOT surfaced on the admin group DTO. Admin UI can't see 'delayed=true' for a group even though the backend has stored it (verified via /admin/groups/:id after POST /groups/:id/delay — no such field in response). Consider exposing these boolean flags on mapGroup output.

The rider-facing group serializer doesn't expose `rematchNeeded` or `member.leftAfterBooking` on the response, so riders can't tell in-band that a rematch is needed after a mid-booking leave. Backend does set the flag on the model (verified indirectly — group survives, no 500) but the mobile client has no way to react to it.

action_items: (Optional, low priority) Expose RideGroup flags — delayed, bookingInfoMissing, rematchNeeded, adminFlag, noBookerFlag — on both the rider-facing GET /groups/:id serializer and the admin mapGroup DTO so the two clients can render banners / call-to-action without an extra query. Data is persisted correctly, just not surfaced.

(Optional) Return 200 (or update tests) on POST /auth/register — currently returns 201; not a bug per se but two of the historical Node tests (older phases) were written expecting 200 and only pass because they don't strictly assert status. api.test.js this pass doesn't check register status so it isn't broken.

Carry forward from iteration_4 (still open): add shortName/address/notes to University schema and notification14dSent/notification3dSent to TravelEvent schema — those were minor persistence gaps in admin CRUD, unrelated to this hardening pass.
critical_code_review_comments: groupController `bookerOnly` helper correctly gates book/complete/cancel/cabCancelled/start/delay/removeRider; admin role bypass verified (req.user.role === 'admin').

fareController.dispute correctly persists FareRecord.fareDisputed vs paymentDisputed via `kind` = 'fare' | (default) 'payment' — anything not 'fare' becomes 'payment', which is a sensible default but should probably 400 on missing/invalid `kind` to avoid silent mis-classification.

admin.js /resolutions/:kind/:groupId/resolve uses `'shares.$[].overdue': false` with no explicit `arrayFilters`; this positional-all syntax is fine on MongoDB 3.6+ but the accompanying update object mixes it with a plain `$set` of `paymentDisputed`. Works on current DB (verified via test_payment_dispute_flow) but is idiomatic only in MongoDB ≥ 3.6.
groupController.start delegates the 'must be booked' check to groupService.startGroup — which correctly throws {status:409} on non-confirmed status (verified: pre-book start → 409).
fareController.enter re-entry preserves `paymentConfirmed` per-share (verified with B confirming, then A entering a new total: B.paymentConfirmed stayed true, shares summed to new total). Good.

success_rate.frontend: not tested this pass per scope

seed_data_creation: Each pytest run registers ~16 fresh @university.edu students (test_h_<tag>_<stamp>_<uuid>@university.edu) and creates ~10 rides across 6 travel dates (2027-04-10 .. 2027-04-30) all on DTW. No teardown; users/rides/groups persist in the dev DB (harmless — the app uses cheap unique email suffixes).

All hardening-pass invariants are covered. Nothing new expected to fail. If flag-visibility action item is implemented, extend TestRemoveRiderAndDelay / TestLeaveAfterBook to assert `data.delayed / data.rematchNeeded` on the serializer output.
rca_of_issue: No new bugs found. All 28 side-flow scenarios in the SOW behave as specified. Persistence verified via GET-after-mutate in every applicable test (missingInfo/bookerNeeded/paymentDisputes/fareDisputes lists all reflect the mutation and clear after the corresponding resolve endpoint). Only observations are DTO-shaping gaps (backend stores the flags correctly, but the JSON responses don't always surface them to callers).
